text.overview: The original 1952 first-ascent line up Chianti Spire, gained by rappelling into the Burgundy-Chianti notch and climbing the peak's north side on then-loose rock; now rarely repeated in favor of the East Face/Rebel Yell.
text.descent: Downclimb or make a short rappel off the summit block back onto the north face, then reverse the line to the Burgundy-Chianti notch. From the notch, traverse north on snow beneath Burgundy Spire's east face and climb the 200-300 ft back up to Burgundy Col - this re-ascent is the sting in the tail and is much easier on firm morning snow than on afternoon slush or bare, sandy rock. name: East Ridge (Prusik Pass)

text.approach: Reach Prusik Pass either from the west (Stuart Lake TH -> Colchuck Lake -> Aasgard Pass -> across the core Enchantment basin) or from the north/east via the longer Snow Creek/Snow Lakes trail (FST 1553) and the upper basin. From Prusik Pass, head west onto Enchantment Peak's east ridge.
text.road: {"name":"Icicle Creek Road (FR 76) to Eightmile Rd (FR 7601), or Icicle Creek Rd to the Snow Lakes TH","status":"Paved then gravel; normally passable to passenger cars in season","driveNote":"Via the Colchuck/Stuart side: from US-2 in Leavenworth, drive Icicle Creek Road 8.4 mi, turn onto Eightmile Rd/FR 7601, and continue 3.8 mi to the Stuart Lake Trailhead.","seasonalGate":"Access roads to these trailheads are typically gated in winter"}
text.overview: The most-traveled, standard line up Enchantment Peak: reach Prusik Pass from the core Enchantment basin, then work west along the peak's east ridge over a couple of minor humps to a short, exposed 3rd-class step onto the small, flat true summit block.
text.descent: Downclimb the short 3rd-class step off the summit block carefully, then walk the ridge's minor humps back east to Prusik Pass. From there, descend the same way you came in — either back over Aasgard Pass to Colchuck Lake, or out via the Snow Lakes trail if approached from that side.
